title: Sushi Emoji 🍣 Meaning: Nigiri, Date Nights and Omakase
description: The sushi emoji 🍣 shows nigiri, raw fish on rice. It means sushi dinners, Japanese food and treat-yourself nights. Uses, pairings and how it differs from 🍱.
summary: 🍣 shows nigiri sushi, a slice of raw fish pressed onto a small block of vinegared rice. People use it to mean sushi itself, a Japanese meal out, a date or birthday dinner, or a craving. It has no established slang meaning; its uses are about food, occasions and taste.
meaning: The emoji is a food order before it is anything else. “🍣 tonight?” proposes a specific kind of evening: a bit more special than pizza, often a little more expensive, and usually shared. People send it to pick a restaurant, to report that takeout has arrived, or to answer the eternal question of what they want for their birthday dinner. It also stands in for cravings, especially among people who say they could eat sushi every day.

Because sushi sits at the pricier end of casual dining in many countries, 🍣 has picked up a treat-yourself shade. A plate photo captioned with it can mean a payday, a celebration or a first date that went well. Food posts use it for omakase counters, where the chef chooses each piece, and for conveyor-belt restaurants, where plates travel past diners on a moving track. In both cases the emoji works as the category tag for the post.

It is also a stand-in for Japanese food and culture more broadly, together with the bento box, the rice ball and the chopsticks. Travelers to Tokyo post it from fish markets and tiny counter bars. Outside Japan it covers local styles too: California rolls, spicy tuna, salmon-heavy menus and supermarket trays. The glyph shows nigiri, but nobody objects when it labels a roll or a poke bowl.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends and couples use it to settle dinner plans in one character. A reply of 🍣🍣 means an enthusiastic yes. It is also a common answer to “what do you want?” on birthdays and anniversaries, which gives it a slightly celebratory feel compared with burgers or fries. Group chats use it to coordinate all-you-can-eat outings, where the goal is volume rather than refinement.

contexts.label: In food captions
contexts.body: Restaurant reviewers, food bloggers and sushi bars tag posts with 🍣 alongside 🥢 and 🍶. It labels tasting menus, new openings and homemade attempts at rolling maki. Restaurants put it in menus, delivery app listings and promotions. Because the glyph shows salmon or tuna nigiri on most platforms, it reads as raw fish first, though people use it for vegetarian rolls as well.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In Japan sushi ranges from everyday supermarket packs to expensive counter meals, and it often appears at family gatherings and celebrations. In North America, Brazil and Europe it has become ordinary takeout with local twists, like cream cheese rolls or mango toppings. The same emoji covers all of these, so its meaning shifts from luxury to weeknight convenience depending on who sends it.

confusedWith.difference: 🍱 is a compartmentalized boxed lunch with rice and several side dishes. It means a packed or takeout meal in general, while 🍣 specifically means pieces of sushi.

🍙 is onigiri, a triangle of rice wrapped in seaweed, sold as a cheap snack at Japanese convenience stores. It contains rice and fillings but is not sushi, since the rice is not vinegared or topped with fish.
🐟 is a live fish and is used for fishing, aquariums and the ocean. Use 🍣 when the fish is on a plate and about to be eaten raw.

avoid: Skip it in messages to someone who keeps a strictly plant-based diet if you mean a raw-fish meal, since it reads as fish.
Avoid using it as a generic symbol for East Asian people or cultures beyond Japanese food, which can come across as stereotyping.
Do not rely on it alone to suggest a restaurant to a group with seafood allergies; name the place and the menu.
design: The glyph shows nigiri: an oblong mound of white rice topped with a slice of raw fish, typically salmon orange or tuna red, and sometimes a strip of nori or a shrimp beside it. Most platforms present it as one or two pieces on a plate or wooden board. The idea is consistent everywhere, with only the fish color and number of pieces changing.

faqs.q: What kind of sushi is the 🍣 emoji?
faqs.a: It depicts nigiri, hand-pressed rice topped with a slice of fish. It is not a roll, though people use it for all sushi, including maki, California rolls and hand rolls. There is no separate emoji for a roll.

faqs.q: Does 🍣 have a slang or flirty meaning?
faqs.a: Not a widespread one. It mostly means sushi, a meal out or Japanese food. Suggesting sushi to a crush is a common low-pressure date idea, so it can appear in flirty plans, but the emoji itself is not innuendo.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🍣 and 🍱?
faqs.a: 🍣 is sushi on its own. 🍱 is a bento, a boxed meal with rice and several dishes in compartments. Sushi can be part of a bento, but the bento emoji usually means a packed lunch or a takeout box.

faqs.q: Is there a sake emoji to go with sushi?
faqs.a: Yes. 🍶 shows a sake bottle and small cup, and it is the usual drink paired with 🍣 in restaurant posts. Green tea 🍵 is the other common pairing, especially for lunch.

faqs.q: When was the sushi emoji added?
faqs.a: 🍣 was part of the original Japanese carrier emoji sets and entered the Unicode standard in 2010. It has been available on all major phones since the early 2010s.
